# What this document does

`catcheR_10Xcatch` reads the CATCHER cassette off the 3' end of `R1 + revcomp(R2)`
as `[barcode 8][UCI 6][reference 23]`, taking the cell ID from a fixed slice of
10X R1 (`cut -c 1-16`) and the UMI from `cut -c 17-28`.

PIPseq breaks the fixed-slice assumption: the cell barcode is built from four
tiers separated by constant linkers and preceded by 0–3 phasing bases, so the
fields are not at fixed offsets. This document is the PIPseq equivalent —
`catcheR_pipcatch` — run end to end on one library, producing every QC table and
figure in `r params$outdir`.

**Run time.** One pass over an 18 M read-pair library takes roughly 20–40 min in
base R. The streaming chunk is cached (`cache = TRUE`); set `max_reads` in the
YAML header to a few million for a fast dry run.

```{r step0-params}
tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("R1", "R2", "reference", "empty reference", "constant",
                "UCI length", "barcode length", "percentage", "ratio", "UMI count"),
  value = c(basename(params$fastq_r1), basename(params$fastq_r2),
            params$reference, params$empty_reference, params$constant,
            params$uci_length, params$barcode_length,
            params$percentage, params$ratio, params$umi_count)
) |> kable(caption = "Run parameters")
```

# Step 1 — Construct geometry

The cassette sits between the vector's MluI site and the reference. In forward
construct orientation:

```
... GCTGATCAG CGAGCTACGCGT [barcode 8] [UCI 6] GGCGCGT TCATCTGGGGGAGCCG
                           \_______ 21 nt insert ________/
```

Because R2 is sequenced from the enrichment primer, it reads the reverse
complement of this, so the construct fields land at *fixed* offsets at the start
of R2 — that part of the 10X design carries over unchanged.

```{r step1-geometry}
revcomp <- function(x) vapply(strsplit(chartr("ACGTN", "TGCAN", x), NULL),
                              function(z) paste(rev(z), collapse = ""), character(1))

REF      <- params$reference
RCREF    <- revcomp(REF)                    # expected at R2 positions 1-23
RC_EMPTY <- revcomp(params$empty_reference) # no-insertion junction
ANCH     <- substr(RCREF, 1, 15)            # invariant part, also the primer 3' end
CONST    <- params$constant                 # vector sequence 3' of the barcode
UL <- params$uci_length; BL <- params$barcode_length

tibble::tibble(
  `R2 position` = c("1-15", "16-23", paste0("24-", 23 + UL),
                    paste0(24 + UL, "-", 23 + UL + BL), paste0(24 + UL + BL, "+")),
  content = c(ANCH, substr(RCREF, 16, 23), "revcomp(UCI)", "revcomp(barcode)", CONST),
  note = c("invariant; shared with the enrichment primer",
           "discriminator: AACGCGCC = barcoded, AACGCGTA = empty",
           paste(UL, "nt"), paste(BL, "nt"), "constant vector")
) |> kable(caption = "Verified R2 layout")
```

**The empty reference must be tested first.** When no cassette is inserted the
flanks fuse and regenerate `` `r params$empty_reference` ``. That junction also
regenerates `CONST` 14 nt earlier than normal, so a classifier that searches for
`CONST` before testing the empty reference silently files empty-vector reads as
"unknown barcode".

# Step 2 — PIPseq read 1 layout

Read 1 is the cell barcode, not construct sequence. After stripping 0–3 phasing
bases the layout is:

```
[phase 0-3] bc1(8) ATG bc2(6) GAG bc3(6) TCGAG bc4(8) index(3) ACG (dT)n
```

```{r step2-parser}
# Vectorised R1 parser. Returns the 28 nt concatenated 4-tier barcode.
# `valid` requires the three linkers AND the downstream index + ACG + oligo-dT:
# matching the linkers alone admits ~15x more reads, nearly all spurious.
parse_r1 <- function(s1) {
  n <- length(s1); phase <- rep(NA_integer_, n)
  for (p in 0:3) {                                   # smallest phase wins
    hit <- is.na(phase) &
      substr(s1, p +  9, p + 11) == "ATG" &
      substr(s1, p + 18, p + 20) == "GAG" &
      substr(s1, p + 27, p + 31) == "TCGAG"
    phase[which(hit)] <- p
  }
  ok <- !is.na(phase); ph <- ifelse(ok, phase, 0L)
  dT <- substr(s1, ph + 46, ph + 53)
  list(
    linker_only = ok,
    valid = ok & substr(s1, ph + 43, ph + 45) == "ACG" &
            nchar(gsub("[^T]", "", dT)) >= 7,
    cell  = paste0(substr(s1, ph +  1, ph +  8), substr(s1, ph + 12, ph + 17),
                   substr(s1, ph + 21, ph + 26), substr(s1, ph + 32, ph + 39)),
    index = substr(s1, ph + 40, ph + 42)
  )
}
```

> The 3 nt `index` is **not** a UMI. There are only 64 possible values and all of
> them are observed, so it saturates immediately. Every metric below counts
> **reads**, not indexes.

# Step 3 — Classify every read

```{r step3-classifier}
classify_r2 <- function(s2, pos) {
  sim <- integer(length(s2))                         # similarity to the 15 nt anchor
  for (i in seq_len(15)) sim <- sim + (substr(s2, i, i) == substr(ANCH, i, i))
  polyA <- grepl(strrep("A", 10), substr(s2, 1, 45), fixed = TRUE)
  ifelse(startsWith(s2, RC_EMPTY), "empty vector (no insertion)",
  ifelse(pos >= 15,                "cassette",
  ifelse(sim >= 13,
         ifelse(polyA, "primer + poly-A chimera", "primer, no cassette, no poly-A"),
         ifelse(polyA, "non-construct insert (poly-A)", "non-construct insert"))))
}
```

# Step 4 — Stream the FASTQ pair

```{r step4-stream, cache=TRUE}
stream_pair <- function(f1, f2, chunk = params$chunk_reads, max_reads = params$max_reads) {
  c1 <- gzfile(f1, "r"); c2 <- gzfile(f2, "r")
  on.exit({ close(c1); close(c2) })
  tot <- 0L; done <- 0
  cls_tot <- integer(0); cell_cls <- list(); cassette <- list(); k <- 0L
  repeat {
    l1 <- readLines(c1, n = chunk * 4L); if (!length(l1)) break
    l2 <- readLines(c2, n = chunk * 4L)
    s1 <- l1[seq(2, length(l1), 4)]; s2 <- l2[seq(2, length(l2), 4)]
    tot <- tot + length(s1); k <- k + 1L

    pr  <- parse_r1(s1); keep <- which(pr$valid)
    v2  <- s2[keep]; pos <- regexpr(CONST, v2, fixed = TRUE)
    cls <- classify_r2(v2, pos)
    cell <- pr$cell[keep]

    cls_tot <- { t <- table(cls); u <- union(names(cls_tot), names(t))
                 setNames(replace(numeric(length(u)), match(names(cls_tot), u), cls_tot) +
                          replace(numeric(length(u)), match(names(t), u), as.numeric(t)), u) }
    cell_cls[[k]] <- as.data.frame(table(cell = cell, cls = cls), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
                     dplyr::filter(Freq > 0)
    j <- which(cls == "cassette")
    if (length(j))
      cassette[[k]] <- data.frame(
        cellID  = cell[j],
        index   = pr$index[keep][j],
        UCI_rc  = substr(v2[j], pos[j] - UL - BL, pos[j] - BL - 1L),
        bc_rc   = substr(v2[j], pos[j] - BL,      pos[j] - 1L),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    done <- done + length(s1)
    if (done >= max_reads) break
  }
  list(total_pairs = tot, class_counts = cls_tot,
       cell_class  = bind_rows(cell_cls) |> count(cell, cls, wt = Freq, name = "n"),
       cassette    = bind_rows(cassette))
}

st <- stream_pair(params$fastq_r1, params$fastq_r2)
st$cassette$UCI     <- revcomp(st$cassette$UCI_rc)
st$cassette$barcode <- revcomp(st$cassette$bc_rc)
cat(sprintf("read pairs: %s | reads with a validated cell barcode: %s | distinct cell barcodes: %s\n",
            format(st$total_pairs, big.mark = ","),
            format(sum(st$class_counts), big.mark = ","),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(st$cell_class$cell), big.mark = ",")))
```

# Step 5 — Reference barcodes and their orientation

The two pooled experiments ship as separate CSVs **written in opposite
orientations**. Rather than hardcode which one needs reverse-complementing, the
orientation is resolved against the reads themselves.

```{r step5-reference}
obs <- unique(st$cassette$barcode)
refs <- lapply(seq_along(params$ref_csv), function(i) {
  r <- read.csv(params$ref_csv[i], header = FALSE, col.names = c("barcode", "shRNA"),
                strip.white = TRUE, colClasses = "character")
  r$barcode <- toupper(trimws(r$barcode))
  hit_fwd <- sum(r$barcode %in% obs); hit_rc <- sum(revcomp(r$barcode) %in% obs)
  if (hit_rc > hit_fwd) { r$barcode <- revcomp(r$barcode); orient <- "reverse-complemented" }
  else orient <- "as given"
  r$set <- params$set_names[i]; r$csv_orientation <- orient
  message(sprintf("%s: %d barcodes, %s (fwd hits %d, rc hits %d)",
                  params$set_names[i], nrow(r), orient, hit_fwd, hit_rc))
  r
})
ref <- bind_rows(refs)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(ref$barcode)))          # no collisions after merging
ref <- ref |> mutate(gene = sub("_[^_]*$", "", shRNA),
                     idx  = suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub(".*_", "", shRNA))),
                     construct = shRNA)
dup <- ref |> count(shRNA) |> filter(n > 1) |> pull(shRNA)
ref$construct[ref$shRNA %in% dup] <- paste0(ref$shRNA[ref$shRNA %in% dup],
                                            " (", ref$set[ref$shRNA %in% dup], ")")
write_csv(ref[, c("barcode", "shRNA")], op("rc_barcodes_genes_merged.csv"), col_names = FALSE)
ref |> count(set, csv_orientation, name = "barcodes") |>
  kable(caption = "Orientation resolved against the reads")
```

> Controls (`B2M`, `SCR1`, `SCR2`, `LUCIFERASE`, `ARHGDIA`) exist in **both**
> CSVs with different barcodes. Always count constructs as `(set, shRNA)` pairs —
> counting by `shRNA` name alone merges them.

# Step 6 — Read-class summary

```{r step6-classes}
T_reads <- st$cassette |> left_join(ref, by = "barcode")
assigned_cells <- unique(T_reads$cellID[!is.na(T_reads$shRNA)])

cls_tab <- tibble::enframe(st$class_counts, name = "class", value = "reads") |>
  mutate(reads = as.integer(reads),
         class = ifelse(class == "cassette", "cassette (split below)", class))
split_cass <- c("assigned" = sum(!is.na(T_reads$shRNA)),
                "cassette present, barcode not in reference" = sum(is.na(T_reads$shRNA)))
read_class <- bind_rows(cls_tab |> filter(class != "cassette (split below)"),
                        tibble::enframe(split_cass, name = "class", value = "reads") |>
                          mutate(reads = as.integer(reads))) |>
  arrange(desc(reads)) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * reads / sum(reads), 2))
write_csv(read_class, op("pipcatch_read_class_summary.csv"))
kable(read_class, caption = "Fate of every read carrying a validated cell barcode")
```

The 16–20 nt primer dimer that dominates the raw library is **absent** here: it
carries no cell barcode at all. Among barcoded molecules the failure mode is the
enrichment primer priming on polyadenylated cDNA, which size selection will not
remove.

# Step 7 — What the no-call cells contain

```{r step7-nocall, fig.height=3.2, fig.width=10}
# Split the "cassette" bucket per READ (a cell can hold both kinds), then pick each
# cell's dominant class. Ties are broken by a FIXED priority, not by row order, so
# the result does not depend on the order reads happened to arrive.
CLASS_PRIORITY <- c("assigned", "cassette present, barcode not in reference",
                    "empty vector (no insertion)", "primer + poly-A chimera",
                    "primer, no cassette, no poly-A", "non-construct insert (poly-A)",
                    "non-construct insert")
cass_split <- T_reads |>
  transmute(cell = cellID,
            cls = ifelse(is.na(shRNA), "cassette present, barcode not in reference", "assigned")) |>
  count(cell, cls, name = "n")
cell_class <- bind_rows(filter(st$cell_class, cls != "cassette"), cass_split)
den  <- n_distinct(cell_class$cell)
asn  <- length(assigned_cells)
nocall <- cell_class |> filter(!cell %in% assigned_cells) |>
  mutate(prio = match(cls, CLASS_PRIORITY)) |>
  group_by(cell) |> arrange(desc(n), prio, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(1) |> ungroup() |>
  count(cls, name = "cells") |> arrange(desc(cells)) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * cells / sum(cells), 1))

uci_cell <- T_reads |> filter(!is.na(shRNA)) |> distinct(cellID, barcode, UCI) |>
  count(cellID, name = "n_UCI")
uci_tab <- uci_cell |> count(n_UCI, name = "cells") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * cells / sum(cells), 1))

pA <- ggplot(uci_tab, aes(factor(n_UCI), cells)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2E6E8E", width = .6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(cells, big.mark = ",")), vjust = -.4, size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10() + labs(x = "distinct UCIs in the cell", y = "cells",
                         title = sprintf("%s cells with a call", format(asn, big.mark = ",")))
pB <- ggplot(nocall, aes(cells, reorder(cls, cells))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#B4432F", width = .65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(cells, big.mark = ","), pct)),
            hjust = -.08, size = 2.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .28))) +
  labs(x = "cells (classified by their dominant read)", y = NULL,
       title = sprintf("%s cells without a call", format(den - asn, big.mark = ",")))
fig_nocall <- pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2))
ggsave(op("pipcatch_nocall_fates.png"), fig_nocall, width = 10, height = 3.2, dpi = 300)
fig_nocall
```

# Step 8 — Per-read assignments

```{r step8-assignments}
# One row per READ. The 3 nt index is carried for reference but is NOT used to
# deduplicate: with only 64 possible values it collides constantly, and collapsing
# on it would silently discard real molecules.
assign_tbl <- T_reads |> filter(!is.na(shRNA)) |>
  select(cell = cellID, idx = index, barcode, UCI, shRNA, set, gene)
write_csv(assign_tbl, op("pipcatch_cell_assignments.csv"))
cat(sprintf("assigned reads: %s | unique (cell, index, barcode, UCI): %s (%.0f%% index collision)\n",
            format(nrow(assign_tbl), big.mark = ","),
            format(nrow(distinct(assign_tbl)), big.mark = ","),
            100 * (1 - nrow(distinct(assign_tbl)) / nrow(assign_tbl))))
head(assign_tbl)
```

# Step 9 — Cell detection and library of origin

The denominator is **validated** PIPseq barcodes seen in R1. It is a
library-quality metric: a cell only enters this library through a read that
reaches the R2 cassette. The fraction of *your* cells that received a
perturbation call must be computed against PIPseeker's called-cell list
(`barcodes.tsv`) from the gene-expression library.

```{r step9-detection, fig.height=2.9, fig.width=9.6}
depth <- assign_tbl |> count(cell, name = "reads") |>
  mutate(bin = cut(reads, c(0, 1, 2, Inf), labels = c("1 read", "2 reads", ">=3 reads"))) |>
  count(bin, name = "cells")
d1 <- tibble::tibble(
  grp = factor(c("shRNA barcode assigned", "no shRNA call"),
               levels = c("shRNA barcode assigned", "no shRNA call")),
  cells = c(asn, den - asn))
pD <- ggplot(d1, aes(x = 1, y = cells, fill = grp)) +
  geom_col(width = .45) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s\n%.1f%%", format(cells, big.mark = ","),
                                100 * cells / den)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = .5), size = 2.6, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E6E8E", "#9AA5AD"), name = NULL) +
  coord_flip() + labs(x = NULL, y = "validated PIPseq cell barcodes in read 1",
                      title = sprintf("%s of %s cell barcodes carry an shRNA call",
                                      format(asn, big.mark = ","), format(den, big.mark = ","))) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
setc <- assign_tbl |> distinct(cell, set) |> count(set, name = "cells") |>
  left_join(tibble::tibble(set = params$set_names, n_shRNA = params$set_sizes), by = "set")
pE <- ggplot(setc, aes(set, cells, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(width = .55, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)\n%.1f per shRNA",
                                format(cells, big.mark = ","),
                                100 * cells / sum(setc$cells), cells / n_shRNA)),
            vjust = -.25, size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E6E8E", "#D1A13A")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .28))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "cells with an shRNA call", title = "Pooled library of origin")
fig_det <- pD + pE + plot_layout(widths = c(1.5, 1))
ggsave(op("pipcatch_cell_detection.png"), fig_det, width = 9.6, height = 2.9, dpi = 300)
fig_det
```

# Step 10 — shRNA detection and clones per shRNA

```{r step10-clones, fig.height=8.2, fig.width=5.4}
clone_summary <- assign_tbl |>
  group_by(set, gene, shRNA) |>
  summarise(clones = n_distinct(UCI), cells = n_distinct(cell), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(clones), desc(cells))
write_csv(clone_summary, op("pipcatch_shRNA_clone_summary.csv"))

grid <- ref |> select(set, gene, shRNA, idx) |>
  left_join(clone_summary, by = c("set", "gene", "shRNA")) |>
  mutate(clones = tidyr::replace_na(clones, 0L), cells = tidyr::replace_na(cells, 0L),
         gene = factor(gene, levels = rev(unique(ref$gene[order(match(ref$set, params$set_names))]))),
         label = ifelse(clones == 0, "n.d.", as.character(clones)))
fig_mat <- ggplot(grid, aes(factor(idx), gene, fill = cells)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, colour = cells > max(grid$cells) * .55), size = 2.1,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08306B", name = "cells") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "#333333")) +
  facet_grid(set ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "shRNA within gene", y = NULL,
       title = sprintf("%d of %d constructs detected, %d clones",
                       sum(grid$clones > 0), nrow(grid), sum(grid$clones)),
       subtitle = "number = distinct clones (UCIs); n.d. = in library, not detected") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
ggsave(op("pipcatch_shRNA_clone_matrix.png"), fig_mat, width = 5.4, height = 8.2, dpi = 300)
fig_mat
```

# Step 11 — Per-cell table

One validated 4-tier barcode = one cell, so reads collapse to one row per cell
before any call is made.

```{r step11-percell}
cu <- assign_tbl |> count(cell, barcode, UCI, shRNA, set, gene, name = "reads")
per_cell <- cu |>
  group_by(cell) |>
  arrange(desc(reads), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(top_barcode = first(barcode), top_UCI = first(UCI), top_shRNA = first(shRNA),
            top_set = first(set), gene = first(gene),
            reads_top = first(reads), reads_second = ifelse(n() > 1, nth(reads, 2), 0L),
            reads_total = sum(reads), n_UCI = n(), n_sets = n_distinct(set),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct_top   = 100 * reads_top / reads_total,
         ratio_top = ifelse(reads_second > 0, reads_top / reads_second, Inf))
write_csv(per_cell, op("pipcatch_per_cell_table.csv"))
tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("cells", "median reads per cell", "max reads per cell",
             "cells with 1 UCI", "cells with 2 UCIs", "cells with >2 UCIs",
             "cells carrying both pooled sets"),
  value  = c(nrow(per_cell), median(per_cell$reads_total), max(per_cell$reads_total),
             sum(per_cell$n_UCI == 1), sum(per_cell$n_UCI == 2), sum(per_cell$n_UCI > 2),
             sum(per_cell$n_sets > 1))
) |> kable(caption = "Per-cell table summary")
```

# Step 12 — catcheR distributions

Equivalents of `barcode_distribution.pdf` and `gene_distribution.pdf`, counting
reads instead of UMIs.

```{r step12-dist, fig.height=6.4, fig.width=10}
bd <- assign_tbl |> left_join(distinct(ref, shRNA, set, construct), by = c("shRNA", "set")) |>
  count(construct, name = "reads") |> arrange(desc(reads))
gd <- assign_tbl |> count(gene, name = "reads") |> arrange(desc(reads))
pbd <- ggplot(bd, aes(reorder(construct, -reads), reads)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2E6E8E") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "reads",
       title = sprintf("barcode distribution - %d constructs detected of %d, %s reads",
                       nrow(bd), nrow(ref), format(nrow(assign_tbl), big.mark = ","))) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = .5, hjust = 1, size = 3.6))
pgd <- ggplot(gd, aes(reorder(gene, -reads), reads)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#D1A13A") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "reads",
       title = sprintf("gene distribution - %d targets (controls pool both sets)", nrow(gd))) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = .5, hjust = 1, size = 5))
fig_dist <- pbd / pgd
ggsave(op("pipcatch_QC_distributions.png"), fig_dist, width = 10, height = 6.4, dpi = 300)
fig_dist
```

# Step 13 — catcheR thresholds

`barcode_silencing_explorative_analysis.R` groups by `(cellID, UCI)`, counts
UMIs, and picks a threshold automatically in one of two modes. Both are
reproduced below on reads.

```{r step13-thresholds}
tab <- cu |> group_by(cell, UCI) |> summarise(readsxUCI = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(cu |> count(cell, wt = reads, name = "readsxcell"), by = "cell") |>
  mutate(pctxUCI = 100 * readsxUCI / readsxcell)

U <- nrow(tab); one <- sum(tab$readsxUCI == 1); perc_1 <- 100 * one / U
p_frac <- perc_1 / 100 * 1.35
thr_noise <- if (p_frac >= 1) NA_integer_ else
  min(sort(tab$readsxUCI, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(ceiling(U * (1 - p_frac)))])

h <- as.data.frame(table(tab$readsxUCI), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(h) <- c("level", "count"); h$level <- as.integer(h$level)
v <- h$count
valley <- if (length(v) >= 3)
  which(c(FALSE, v[-c(1, length(v))] < v[-c(length(v) - 1, length(v))] &
                 v[-c(1, length(v))] <= v[-c(1, 2)], FALSE)) else integer(0)
# NOTE: catcheR uses findValleys(...)[1] as the threshold, i.e. the histogram
# POSITION. That equals the read/UMI count only when levels are contiguous.
# Read the level instead:
thr_bimodal <- if (length(valley)) h$level[valley[1]] else NA_integer_

tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("(cell, UCI) pairs", "pairs with 1 read", "% with 1 read",
               'threshold, mode = "noise"', 'threshold, mode = "bimodal"'),
  value = c(U, one, sprintf("%.1f%%", perc_1),
            ifelse(is.na(thr_noise), "undefined (>74.07% singletons)", thr_noise),
            ifelse(is.na(thr_bimodal), "no valley", thr_bimodal))
) |> kable(caption = "Automatic threshold estimation")
```

> **Guard worth adding to `pipcatch`.** The noise estimator computes
> `p = perc_1/100 * 1.35` and keeps `ceiling(nrow * (1 - p))` rows. Once more
> than 1/1.35 = **74.07%** of pairs are singletons, `1 - p` is negative and the
> subset `UMIxUCI[1:n, ]` errors in R. Refuse with a depth message instead.

## Filtering and validity

```{r step13-filter}
run_filter <- function(thr) {
  t <- tab |> mutate(TorF = pctxUCI > params$percentage & readsxUCI > thr) |>
    group_by(cell) |> mutate(True_UCIxcellID = sum(TorF)) |> ungroup()
  v <- t |> group_by(cell) |>
    summarise(True_UCIxcellID = first(True_UCIxcellID),
              mx = max(readsxUCI),
              second = if (n() > 1) sort(readsxUCI, decreasing = TRUE)[2] else NA_real_,
              pct_at_max = pctxUCI[which.max(readsxUCI)], .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(ValidCell = True_UCIxcellID == 1 &
             ((!is.na(second) & mx / second >= params$ratio) | pct_at_max == 100))
  list(pairs = t, cells = v)
}
thr_grid <- c(`recommended at this depth` = 0L,
              `catcheR's lowest meaningful value (comparison is strict >)` = 1L)
if (!is.na(thr_bimodal)) thr_grid[['automatic "bimodal" pick']] <- thr_bimodal
filter_returns <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(thr_grid), function(i) {
  r <- run_filter(thr_grid[[i]])
  tibble::tibble(threshold = thr_grid[[i]],
                 TorF_pairs = sum(r$pairs$TorF),
                 cells_with_true_UCI = sum(r$cells$True_UCIxcellID > 0),
                 ValidCell = sum(r$cells$ValidCell),
                 note = names(thr_grid)[i])
}))
write_csv(filter_returns, op("pipcatch_filter_returns.csv"))
kable(filter_returns, caption = "What the filter returns")

res <- run_filter(params$umi_count)
complete_table_fin <- res$pairs |> left_join(res$cells |> select(cell, ValidCell), by = "cell")
write_csv(complete_table_fin, op("pipcatch_complete_table_fin.csv"))
```

```{r step13-fig, fig.height=6.6, fig.width=9.6}
p1 <- ggplot(h, aes(level, count)) + geom_col(fill = "grey45", width = .7) +
  scale_y_log10() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = h$level) +
  { if (!is.na(thr_bimodal)) geom_vline(xintercept = thr_bimodal + .5, colour = "#B4432F") } +
  labs(x = "readsxUCI", y = "(cell, UCI) pairs", title = "readsxUCI (catcheR UMIxUCI)")
p2 <- ggplot(tab, aes(pctxUCI)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "grey45") +
  scale_y_log10() + geom_vline(xintercept = params$percentage, colour = "#B4432F") +
  labs(x = "read percentage x UCI", y = "(cell, UCI) pairs",
       title = sprintf("percentage per UCI (minimum %.0f%%)", min(tab$pctxUCI)))
d2 <- complete_table_fin |> count(pctxUCI, readsxUCI, True_UCIxcellID, ValidCell, name = "n")
p3 <- ggplot(d2, aes(pctxUCI, readsxUCI, size = n, colour = factor(True_UCIxcellID))) +
  geom_point(alpha = .55) + scale_y_log10() + scale_size_area(max_size = 9, guide = "none") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params$percentage, colour = "#B4432F", linewidth = .3) +
  labs(colour = "True_UCIxcellID", title = "coloured by true UCIs per cell")
p4 <- ggplot(d2, aes(pctxUCI, readsxUCI, size = n, colour = ValidCell)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .55) + scale_y_log10() + scale_size_area(max_size = 9, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#D1A13A", `FALSE` = "#8FA8BF")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params$percentage, colour = "#B4432F", linewidth = .3) +
  labs(title = "coloured by ValidCell")
fig_thr <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4) +
  plot_annotation(title = sprintf("threshold %s, percentage %s, ratio %s - %s of %s cells valid",
                                  params$umi_count, params$percentage, params$ratio,
                                  format(sum(res$cells$ValidCell), big.mark = ","),
                                  format(nrow(res$cells), big.mark = ",")),
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 9)))
ggsave(op("pipcatch_QC_thresholds.png"), fig_thr, width = 9.6, height = 6.6, dpi = 300)
fig_thr
```

```{r step14-manifest}
tibble::tibble(file = list.files(params$outdir)) |>
  mutate(size_kb = round(file.size(file.path(params$outdir, file)) / 1024, 1)) |>

```

# Known limitations

1. **Barcode error correction is not applied.** Tiers are validated structurally
   but not against PIPseeker's whitelists, so a single error in `bc1` or `bc4`
   creates a barcode that passes and belongs to no real cell. Correct each tier
   against the whitelist, then key on the translated 16 nt cell ID
   (`metrics/barcodes/barcode_whitelist.txt`) — that is what the expression-matrix
   columns use.
2. **No UMI deduplication.** The 3 nt index is not a UMI; confirm the chemistry
   (`pipseeker --chemistry v3/v4/v5`).
3. **`catcheR_nocatch` cannot run at this depth.** Empty-vector reads are far too
   few to populate a negative-control set, and a cell with no call is far more
   likely to have lost its construct read to primer mispriming.
4. **Depth, not thresholds, is the limit.** Fixing the dimer by size selection
   and the mispriming by a nested or higher-stringency enrichment PCR are the two
   levers; the automatic threshold modes become usable again once the
   `readsxUCI` histogram develops a genuine valley.
